lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Check that the LinkedIn URL works.
Check that the email and phone number are appropriate for applications.
Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requires them.
items.because: They generally do not help assess your qualifications.

items.says: Check that the university and degree names match your official records.
Consider omitting the date range.
items.because: It is optional at this career stage.

items.says: Put Stonebridge before Crescent Bank.
items.because: Your most recent experience should appear first.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration would generally increase, not hedge, interest-rate exposure.
Substantiate the claim of no rise in early defaults.
items.because: The comparison period and whether approved loans had enough time to season are unclear.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
Clarify whether the reduction from seven missed tests to one is measured annually.
items.because: It could instead be a projection.

items.says: Specify whether the six-to-three-hour saving covers a full credit memo or only spreading.
Identify a consistently measured forecast-error metric for “under 4%."
Clarify that the forecast materially supported the early debt repayment.
items.because: The forecast may have merely coincided with it.

items.says: Ensure the 30 items were actually automated.
Ensure the five-day close is a sustained result.
Add a decision or operational outcome if one exists.
items.because: Standardizing assumptions does not show what happened as a result.

items.says: Fix the mixed “Mapping … cut” construction.
items.because: The action and result need to be grammatically connected.

items.says: Verify that the reduction in journal entries is attributable to this work.
Discounting free cash flow to equity at weighted average cost of capital mixes an equity cash flow with an enterprise discount rate.
Add a measured adoption or efficiency result if one exists.
Verify that “Nov 2024 – Present” still reflects active project work.
Avoid implying that proximity to the market price validates the model.
items.because: Being within 6% is a comparison, not proof the valuation was accurate.

items.says: A fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is 20%, not 25%.
Confirm that “1 point” means one percentage point in the discount rate.
Clarify what was forecast and what “accuracy” means.
Explain how the forecast was tested without using information unavailable at the forecast date.
Moving from 70% to 82% is 12 percentage points, not a 12% relative increase.
Identify the group supported accurately.
items.because: “FP&A team” sounds inconsistent with a student investment fund unless it had one.

items.says: Make the bullet more specific.
items.because: It is less specific than your other work.

items.says: Identify the benchmark if it helps establish the comparison's rigor.
Treat the onboarding-notes bullet as lower priority if space is needed.
items.because: It shows less finance impact than the performance-report bullet.

items.says: List additional tools if you used them and can use them confidently.
items.because: “Excel” alone undersells the work suggested by your experience.

items.says: Keep only methods you can defend in an interview, particularly DCF valuation.
